live_clock_anomaly.reading: the day/night fraction moved by 0.35 while worldTime advanced 1.33 days, so the fraction is NOT the naive fmod(worldTime, 900)/900 - recorded as an open discrepancy against the simple reading of the clock model

live_craftable_objects.resolution: the class object is relocated from the ELF's __objc_classlist through the live rw segment and cross-checked against the relocated classlist cell (both agree), rather than being read from the OBJC_CLASS_$_ symbol slot - an earlier attempt did the latter and 'found' 18 hits that were entries in the library's own pointer tables
live_craftable_objects.observation: one instance (0x67d65df4) carries small integers in the record (f0=1, f4=1, f9=1, arrays mostly 0 with a few 1s), which is what a crafting record should look like; the other two are pointer-heavy. With three instances no generalisation is claimed - the value here is that live records are now readable and reproducible.

boundary: three instances at one moment in one save. Nothing here names a field; the values are recorded as read.

instance_identification_negative.what_was_tried: find instances by scanning anonymous rw regions for a word equal to the class pointer, for both Action (reading interactionTestResult @52, modelled as iiSS) and CraftableItemObject
instance_identification_negative.class_resolution_is_sound: Action -> 0x67127d84 and CraftableItemObject -> 0x67128cac, both agreeing with the relocated __objc_classlist cell
instance_identification_negative.but_the_criterion_is_not: only three words matched per class, and their contents do not match the layouts the encodings declare: CraftableItemObject's records show pointers inside the int[8] array ranges, and Action's interactionTestResult decodes as pointers rather than iiSS. So 'first word == class pointer' still matches class references held elsewhere (tables, caches) rather than instances
instance_identification_negative.conclusion: the heap scan is replaced, not patched: the right route is to WALK THE OBJECT GRAPH from a root that can be identified with a strong signature - _validate_world does exactly that (header class, DynamicWorld hop, backref, saveID string) - and this project's world_layout.h with its 227 named ivar offsets is the map for that walk. The deliverable becomes the tool.

deeper walking found nothing more, and inspecting PaintMixUI's 28 ivars shows only ONE pointer to a known class: its world backref. The idle paint-mix UI holds no workbench and no craftable object - which is exactly why the record is not here to read

anomaly_sharpened.before: timeOfDayFraction moved 0.354 while worldTime advanced 1.33 days, so the fraction is not fmod(worldTime, 900)/900
anomaly_sharpened.now: at this snapshot the fraction reads 0.2286 while the sun's Y component is ~0.0094, i.e. the sun is essentially on the horizon - the phase and the sun agree with each other. So the fraction IS a day phase (~0.25 = sunrise); what disagrees is its rate against worldTime
anomaly_sharpened.falsifiable_next_question: which counter advances the phase? The fraction is consistent with the sun and inconsistent with worldTime/900, so either a second counter exists or the fraction is derived per frame with a different constant - both are answerable statically now that the question is that specific.

live_world_rate_table.method: sample every numeric World ivar twice, 25.001 s apart, and report units/second (the probe reuses the validated Probe class; read-only)
semantics_earned_from_rates: isHeadingTowardsMIdday is a one-byte DIRECTION flag for the day phase (it toggles 1 -> 0 in this window, and its name is in the World layout this project already derived) - a meaning the live rates give and the static reading could not
noRainTimer advances with worldTime and carries worldTime's magnitude (459607 -> 460104 against 461585 -> 462085), so it is the same clock domain expressed as seconds, not an independent timer
slowAnimationIndex and waterAnimationIndex advance by WRAPPING (14 -> 0, 12 -> 0), which is what frame-cycled animation counters look like

saveCount and saveCounter are DIFFERENT fields with different rates (0.99996/s vs 0.19999/s) and this also corrects an earlier note of mine that read saveCounter as decreasing: live data says it increments

anomaly_answered.question: which counter advances the day phase? (recorded last batch as falsifiable)
anomaly_answered.answer: not worldTime. The phase advances 0.01183/s while worldTime advances 20/s - a ratio of about 1:1690 worldTime units per full phase, whereas a naive 900-units-per-day reading would put it at 1:900. So a second counter or a different constant exists, and the static search now has a target rather than a mystery

live_day_phase_measured.method: sample timeOfDayFraction, isHeadingTowardsMIdday, sunDirection.y and worldTime every 2 s for 96 s (offsets resolved by NAME through the ivar table, not hand-copied)

findings.shape: the fraction is a TRIANGLE wave between ~0.002 and ~0.476, not a monotone 0..1 day cycle: it rose to 0.476, turned, fell to 0.002, and turned again inside the window
findings.flag_meaning: isHeadingTowardsMIdday is 1 while the phase RISES and 0 while it FALLS - it is literally 'the phase is increasing', and it flips exactly at the turning points (1->0 at 0.476, 0->1 at 0.002)
findings.period: half period ~1320 worldTime units and a full cycle ~2640 units (about 132 s at the observed 20 units/s)
findings.independence_from_the_sun: sun_y decreased monotonically through the whole window (+0.081 -> -0.372) while the phase oscillated, so the two are independent

correction_of_my_own_earlier_claim.earlier: 'at this snapshot the fraction reads 0.2286 while the sun's Y component is ~0.0094, i.e. the sun is essentially on the horizon - the phase and the sun agree with each other'
correction_of_my_own_earlier_claim.now: WRONG, and the samples show why: the sun's Y is monotone while the fraction is a triangle, so 0.2286 with sun_y ~0 was a coincidence of that instant. The phase is not derived from the sun.
correction_of_my_own_earlier_claim.what_replaces_it: the phase is its own triangle wave with a measured period; the flag reports its direction. Both are now measured rather than read off a single sample.

live_day_phase_measured.supersedes: the previous batch's derivation of 'about 1690 worldTime units per full phase' - that number came from a 60 s delta that contained a turnaround, so it was an average over a fold, not a period. The triangle measurement replaces it.

craft_path_probe.why: BFS found nothing deeper and reported that as 'nothing found'; following the KNOWN ivar path instead shows exactly which hop is null, which is the difference between 'not reachable' and 'not loaded'
path_verified: PaintMixUI +20 world        -> World       0x61f96000  (backref, closes the loop)
craft_path_probe.reading: the paint-mix UI object exists and is wired to the World, but every crafting-related ivar is null: no workbench screen is open, so no craftable object has been bound. The path is proven and the fields that will hold the record are identified - this is a state question, not a mechanism one

ready_when_the_state_is_loaded.then: re-run live175/probe_craft_path.py; any non-null CraftableItemObject on that path has its 124-byte record read inline at its own ivar offset and decoded against the model

why_the_objc_walk_stops_here.evidence: DynamicWorld's ivar table: dynamicObjects @60, dynamicObjectsToAdd @840, dynamicObjectsByWorldPosIndex @1620, freeBlocksByPosition @2400 - the strides are exactly 780 bytes, so these are INLINE C++ containers rather than Objective-C objects
why_the_objc_walk_stops_here.consequence: the world's dynamic objects (Workbench among them) live inside those containers, so an ObjC-graph walk that follows ivars and checks isas will ALWAYS stop in front of them. That is the mechanistic reason the BFS reported 'nothing deeper', not a wrong path
why_the_objc_walk_stops_here.what_it_would_take: decoding an inline C++ container's internal layout (libc++ or custom) to enumerate its elements - a project of its own, and not needed for the crafting record: opening the workbench screen binds PaintMixUI.workbench (1 hop) and the record becomes readable
why_the_objc_walk_stops_here.consequence_for_the_plan: the live route to the crafting record is the one hop that the game state provides, while the container route would be a large detour. That settles which one to wait for.

static_scan_vs_live_contradiction.conclusion: the static scan reports no writer for a field that demonstrably changes, and no reference at all for a field it can read - so this family's per-ivar coverage has a CONFIRMED gap, and the contradiction comes from live data rather than from a hunch. For these fields the live read is the authority and the cell scan's silence is not evidence of absence.
static_scan_vs_live_contradiction.why_this_matters: it is the same failure mode as the fused-store gap (a tool limitation read as a property of the binary), but this time the counter-example is a measurement rather than a reasoned suspicion - which is what makes it worth recording separately
candidates_for_the_missing_writer: a store through a computed pointer (the C++ side writing a field of a World-like struct)
a store form the classifier still does not recognise
the value being derived per frame from another quantity rather than stored - in which case the ivar would only be written by whatever caches it, and the scan should have seen that too
